summary: i386 programs on the x86-64 kernel where no other family has a case of them: mixprobe's calls between an i386 and an x86-64 program on the x86-64 kernel, and the i686 probes of i386's own interfaces, ldtprobe and drmcompatprobe, which the ia32 profile runs on the x86-64 kernel; lockstressmusl, whose i686 build the profile runs on the x86-64 kernel beside its x86-64 build, for the paths taken off the big lock on both entries; the i686 builds of the other probes are the cases of their own families, which the profile runs there too

cases.behavior: On the x86-64 kernel an i386 program and an x86-64 program exec each other, pass descriptors by SCM_RIGHTS, share a futex, trace each other, run under each other's seccomp filters and queue signals to each other, each seeing the other's calls and records in its own ABI's layout, as on Linux

execution.cleanup: the probe removes what it made

assertions.checks: an execve of /ia32/mixprobe runs it in CS 0x23 with its argument and environment vectors whole
the i386 execve of /mixprobe runs it in CS 0x33 with its vectors whole
the i386 execveat of mixprobe through a descriptor of the root runs it in CS 0x33 with its vectors whole
a pipe's read end that the i386 program sends by SCM_RIGHTS arrives in a control message of x86-64's layout, cmsg_len 20 and msg_controllen 24, and reads what the sender wrote
a pipe's read end that the x86-64 program sends by SCM_RIGHTS arrives in a control message of i386's layout, cmsg_len 16 and msg_controllen 16, and reads what the sender wrote
an x86-64 FUTEX_WAKE of a word of a memfd page both map shared wakes one waiter, the i386 FUTEX_WAIT on that word with a 32-bit timespec, which returns 0
an i386 futex_time64 FUTEX_WAKE of another word of the page wakes the x86-64 FUTEX_WAIT on it, which returns 0
an i386 FUTEX_WAIT with a 32-bit timespec of 20 ms, and a futex_time64 FUTEX_WAIT of 20 ms whose tv_nsec has all ones in its upper half, each end with ETIMEDOUT

an x86-64 tracer reads CS 0x23 and an RIP in the i386 text at the i386 tracee's exec stop, and AUDIT_ARCH_I386 with number 20 from PTRACE_GET_SYSCALL_INFO and orig_rax 20 at its getpid's entry stop, and the tracee runs to its end

an i386 tracer, whose tracee the i386 clone3 makes, reads i386's 17-word registers of the x86-64 tracee at its exec stop, xcs 0x33 and eip in the x86-64 text, and AUDIT_ARCH_X86_64 with number 39 and orig_eax 39 at its getpid's entry stop, and the tracee runs to its end
a filter an x86-64 process installs, judging the architecture and the number, returns errno 77 for the i386 getpid of the i386 program it then execs
a filter an i386 process installs in a child of the i386 clone returns errno 78 for the x86-64 getpid of the x86-64 program the child then execs
SIGUSR1 that the x86-64 program queues by rt_sigqueueinfo reaches the i386 program's SA_SIGINFO handler with the sender's pid, SI_QUEUE and its value in i386's siginfo
SIGUSR1 that the i386 program queues by the i386 rt_sigqueueinfo reaches the x86-64 program's SA_SIGINFO handler with the sender's pid, SI_QUEUE and its value in x86-64's siginfo

native.reason: the i386 build runs from /ia32/mixprobe, which only the test image stages

cases.behavior: An i386 program on the x86-64 kernel has modify_ldt and the 32-bit vDSO's __kernel_vsyscall as on Linux's 64-bit kernel; the i686 kernel has no modify_ldt

execution.cleanup: the probe removes what it made

assertions.checks: on the i686 kernel modify_ldt fails with ENOSYS
modify_ldt's read of the default LDT gives 128 zero bytes
a read before any write gives nothing

a write refuses a size other than a user_desc's and an entry past 8191 with EINVAL, a present conforming code segment with EINVAL in both modes, an argument it cannot read with EFAULT and another function with ENOSYS, and takes a conforming one not present and a 16-bit segment
a 32-bit data segment written to entry 3 loads into FS and reads the block it covers
the read gives the entry back as Linux's fill_ldt makes it, with the entries around it zero
the old mode clears the descriptor's AVL bit, which the new mode keeps, and clears the entry for a base and a limit of 0
a far call through a code segment of the LDT runs there with that CS, makes a system call and returns
a child has a copy of the LDT, in which its own write changes nothing of the parent's, and the parent's FS still reads its block after waiting for the child
a signal's return puts back FS's LDT selector, which the handler cleared
clearing an entry leaves ES that held it null at once, and FS null after a sleep
a child whose far call clears its own code segment takes SIGSEGV at the return, and the kernel goes on
AT_SYSINFO names __kernel_vsyscall, through which getpid gives the pid and mmap2, with its page offset in EBP, the second page of a memfd

native.reason: modify_ldt and __kernel_vsyscall are i386's, and the native machine runs the x86-64 build of its programs

ia32.why: the x86-64 kernel gives an i386 program modify_ldt and __kernel_vsyscall, as Linux's does, and the i686 kernel has neither; ldtprobe reports the group kernel from ETUDE_KERNEL, the kernel's architecture

cases.behavior: The DRM requests whose i386 layouts differ from x86-64's, made by an i386 program on QEMU's std-vga, are answered as Linux 6.12's drm_ioc32.c answers them on the x86-64 kernel and natively on the i686 kernel

execution.cleanup: the probe removes what it made

assertions.checks: one of /dev/dri/card0 to card15 opens and answers GET_CAP with DRM_CAP_DUMB_BUFFER set
VERSION, with its lengths and pointers in 4 bytes, gives the driver's name, date and description, their lengths alone and then into buffers, touching no guard byte
GETRESOURCES, whose 64-bit pointers carry 32-bit addresses, counts the CRTCs and connectors and then lists them, each of a nonzero id
ADDFB2, with its modifiers at 68, adds a framebuffer on a dumb buffer of 64 by 64 pixels and gives its id, leaving the request as it was
GETFB2 reads the framebuffer back, its modifiers at 68, and RMFB and DESTROY_DUMB remove it and its buffer
WAIT_VBLANK, relative 0, gives the count and time of the last vblank in its 16 bytes, or EOPNOTSUPP with the request copied back on a card with no vblank interrupt
GET_UNIQUE, GET_CLIENT and GET_STATS use their 8, 24 and 124 byte i386 layouts, including the current pid and zero counters, without writing guard bytes
GETPLANERESOURCES, OBJ_GETPROPERTIES and OBJ_SETPROPERTY use their 12, 28 and 20 byte i386 sizes without copying native tail padding
GET_STATS, SET_UNIQUE and UPDATE_DRAW on a non-DRM descriptor return ENOTTY and on a closed descriptor EBADF

native.reason: the requests' i386 layouts are i386's, and the native machine runs the x86-64 build of its programs

ia32.why: the x86-64 kernel translates the i386 layouts through its compat ioctl path, where the i686 kernel takes them natively; the probe expects the same answers of both

cases.behavior: The paths taken off the big lock, switches and wakes, poll and epoll, close and dup2 under a blocked call, concurrent unmaps, page faults against mapping changes, shared file mappings under truncation, exit and reap, futex requeues, warmed lookups, /proc's snapshots against threads that come and go, and vgem's fences, each raced across four processors, give Linux's answers; with -u, bkl/calls counts no hold of the big lock for the calls named

execution.cleanup: the program joins its threads, reaps every child and removes the file and directory it made in /dev/shm

assertions.checks: pairs of threads, one for each processor and at least two, pass 2000 counts each way through a futex word with FUTEX_WAIT and FUTEX_WAKE and then through two pipes, each side seeing every count in order

a reader polls 64 pipes, and then waits on them in an epoll set, while a writer on each other processor writes 2000 bytes into them; every byte arrives once, from the pipe it was written to, poll and epoll give POLLIN alone, and a pipe given as readable reads at least a byte

400 rounds of a read blocked on a pipe or a write of 256 KiB blocked on a full pipe, whose descriptor another processor closes or replaces by dup2, after no delay, a yield, a spin or 1 ms: a call that began on the file finishes on it, as Linux's filp_close leaves it, and one that began after fails with EBADF or uses the new file

two processes at once unmap and map again a region of 16 pages 500 times while their threads on the other processors read it; every read gives 0, a value of the mapping it read or a later one, never an earlier one or the other process's, or faults in the gap

four threads write and read back their own word of one page while a fifth maps the page afresh, makes it read-only, writable again and unmaps it 500 times, and a child maps and touches half the memory available: each read gives the count written or a fresh page's 0, or faults, and no word changes while the page is read-only

on a shared mapping of a file of 16 pages, two processes read every 64th byte, one writing too, while others write the file 300 times, truncate and grow it again 300 times, and map, write and unmap it 300 times: every byte read is 0 or a letter written; afterwards the mapping reads what the file was written and the file what the mapping was, and a page truncated away and grown again reads as zeros

64 children in batches of 8 exit while a thread of the parent wakes the futex word their own thread sleeps on, and wait4 reaps each once with its own exit code; 200 threads are joined as they end, each giving back its value

two threads requeue 4000 times the waiters of two futex words onto each other with FUTEX_CMP_REQUEUE while four waiters wait on them with timeouts of 1 to 3 ms; every requeue returns a count or EAGAIN, every wait 0, ETIMEDOUT, EAGAIN or EINTR, and every waiter returns

a thread on each processor, at least two, makes newfstatat (fstatat64 for i386) and openat of 16 files 200 times, by a directory's descriptor and by path in turn, after a first stat warmed them, and sees each file's inode, size and three bytes as made

a thread on each processor, at least two, opens and reads whole, in reads of at most 64 bytes, /proc/self/stat, its own /proc/self/task/TID/stat and /proc/stat 300 times and preads at offset 0 a descriptor of /proc/self/stat that another thread dups and closes meanwhile, while a third makes and joins short threads whose task stat files the readers open too: each stat text begins with its process's or thread's id and ends with a newline, /proc/stat begins with its cpu line, and a thread gone fails the open with ENOENT or ESRCH alone

on vgem's primary node a dumb buffer's dma-buf polls readable and writable with no fence and neither with a write fence, a read fence beside it is EBUSY, and while one thread attaches and signals 2000 write fences two attach and signal read fences, EBUSY alone refusing them, and poll the dma-buf; afterwards a write fence attaches and the buffer is idle
over the modes run, debugfs's bkl/calls counts at least one call of each call -u names and no hold of the big lock that an entry of it began
